12.0.s.en: 1. Remember your Creator in the days of your youth:

12.0.0.en: 1 Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, or the years draw near when you say, “I have no pleasure in them.”

12.0.1.en: If the world has become vain because of man's corruption and his life, it is fitting for man to be bound to God from his youth, so that vanities may not deceive him and he may not be confused by its cares... He has already spoken of the motives that drive the young person to enjoy fellowship with God (Eccl 11:7-10), especially the life of true joy. Perhaps a young man will say: Why do I not wait until old age? The Preacher answers him, saying:

12.0.2.en: “Before the evil days come, or the years draw near when you say, I have no pleasure in them” [1].

12.0.3.en: The evil days may come early, as when a person loses consciousness and so loses the possibility of repentance and return to God, or early death may take him suddenly; or the years of old age may come, and a person loses the sweetness of life... He calls us to return immediately to God, that we may experience the sweetness of fellowship with Him.

12.0.4.en: The Psalmist says: “O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I declare Your wondrous works. Even to old age and grey hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I declare Your arm to the coming generation, Your power to everyone who is to come” (Ps 71:17-18).

12.1.s.en: 2. The weakness and troubles of old age:

12.1.0.en: 2 Before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain. 3 In the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows are darkened. 4 And the doors are shut in the market, when the sound of the mill is low, and he rises up at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of music are brought low. 5 Also they are afraid of that which is high, and fears are in the way, and the almond tree flourishes, and the grasshopper is a burden, and desire fails; because man goes to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the market. 6 Before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. 7 Then the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it. 8 Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher: all is vanity.

12.1.1.en: The Preacher describes the dissolution of old age and its infirmities in descriptive expressions that are difficult to grasp now, because they are no longer used, but in general they reveal the distress of the wise Solomon at the days of old age. He gave this description to make clear that a person loses much of his vitality in his old age, so that even if he repents he does not have the capacity for the work of a young person, for his striving, and for his enjoyment of the sweetness of early spiritual life.

12.1.2.en: a. “The sun and the light and the moon and the stars are darkened” [2]. For a person in his old age almost loses his sight, so he thinks the light to be darkness, and it seems to him as if the clouds had drawn the curtain over the stars.

12.1.3.en: Perhaps what is meant here by the sun and the light... is that a person in his old age feels that he has lost the joy of life and its beauty, so the sun has become darkness to him...

12.1.4.en: If a person is struck with spiritual old age, his insight does not behold the Sun of Righteousness, the divine light does not shine upon him, he does not grasp the true concept of the Church as a moon illumined by Christ, and he does not benefit from fellowship with the saints as luminous stars.

12.1.5.en: b. “And the clouds return after the rain” [2]. The clouds here signify the multitude of trials that befall a person in his old age, of sufferings and sicknesses. They are like the cloud that pours down rain and returns again, then a third time, etc...

12.1.6.en: Whoever is struck with spiritual old age feels a dryness that causes him successive falls.

12.2.0.en: c. “In the day when the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men bow themselves” [3]. This points to the weakness of the skeleton and the collapse of the nervous system, so the old man is not strong enough to face physical and psychological health troubles.

12.2.1.en: In spiritual old age, where a person is deprived of the leadership of the Spirit of God who renews our youth like the eagle, a person enters into despair, so that the strong among them becomes like a house without a guard or an army without strength! He collapses before trials and their storms!

12.2.2.en: d. “And the grinders cease because they are few” [3]. The teeth that chew and grind food fall out, so that he is unable even to enjoy many kinds of food.

12.2.3.en: In spiritual old age a person does not experience the words of the Psalmist: “I found Your word sweet, and I ate it,” because he has no spiritual teeth that are able to enjoy spiritual food and feed on it.

12.2.4.en: e. “And those that look out of the windows are darkened” [3]. That is, the senses of the body weaken, so the old man does not respond to what surrounds him.

12.2.5.en: In spiritual old age the inner senses lose their sanctity and grow dark, so they do not behold heavenly things, nor smell the sweet fragrance of Christ, nor know how to utter with the heavenly ones the celestial praises...

12.3.0.en: f. “And the doors are shut in the market” [4]. Old people are unable to go out of their homes even to buy their essential staple food, as if the doors of the market had been shut in their faces.

12.3.1.en: In spiritual old age a person lies hidden in the “ego,” and so finds the gates of heaven shut before him because of the closing of his heart toward God and people. He becomes like one who buried his talent in the earth and did not trade with it.

12.3.2.en: g. “And he rises up at the voice of the sparrow” [4]. Because of their nervous fatigue and lack of movement all day long, they cannot bear the voice of a sparrow, so they rise from their sleep, a sign of their loss of inner rest in the Lord under flimsy excuses such as the chirping of a sparrow.

12.3.3.en: h. “And all the daughters of music are brought low” [4]. They do not share their joys with others because of their weariness, an indication of the deprivation of fellowship in praise and joy with the heavenly ones.

12.4.0.en: i. “Also they are afraid of that which is high” [5]. They do not live on the upper floors lest they fall as they go up or down, an indication of spiritual complacency, and of no desire for spiritual growth and the constant lifting of the heart to eternity.

12.4.1.en: j. “And fears are in the way” [5]. They live in sluggishness; they do not want movement, an indication of no desire for spiritual striving and for enjoying new spiritual experiences.

12.4.2.en: k. “The almond tree flourishes” [5]. An indication of the white hair that fills the head so that it becomes like a blossoming almond tree. It represents the loss of the spiritual vitality of youth.

12.4.3.en: l. “And the grasshopper is a burden” [5]. They are not able to bear even the lightest kinds of food, like the grasshopper, which is a very light food, easy to digest. It signifies finding any spiritual exercise for building up the soul burdensome.

12.4.4.en: m. “And desire fails” [5]. The loss of every inner desire for gladness and joy, an indication that a person loses his spiritual joy, his inner peace, and his longing for heavenly things.

12.4.5.en: n. The old man, as he awaits death to enter his eternal home [5], is likened to: the silver cord that is loosed, that which binds the soul to the body, or the golden bowl that is broken, or a water pitcher that is shattered, or a well pulley that is smashed, that is, he turns into wreckage with no use; it is an approach to the return to dust. And in spiritual old age a person feels that his life is of no use, nearer to dust than to heaven!

12.5.0.en: 9 Furthermore, because the Preacher was wise, he also taught the people knowledge; and he weighed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs. 10 The Preacher sought to find acceptable words, written uprightly, words of truth. 11 The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails fastened, masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd. 12 And furthermore, my son, be warned of these: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh. 13 Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man. 14 For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it be good or evil.

12.5.1.en: The Preacher did not want to draw the curtain on the painful picture of old age, but offered a remedy for overcoming the vanity of temporal life, namely, meeting with God, the Creator of the world and the preparer of eternal glory, through obedience to His commandment with a godly fear.

12.5.2.en: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter:

12.5.3.en: Fear God, and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.

12.6.0.en: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it be good or evil” [13-14].

12.6.1.en: The remedy for the matter is clinging to God through godliness or the righteousness of Christ, who gives the fear mixed with love, so that we may gain our life in Him and enjoy keeping His commandment, awaiting the Day of Judgment as the beginning of a glorious eternal life in place of the vain, passing life.

12.6.2.en: As though his final commandment is: Fear God, and keep His commandments!

12.6.3.en: * The beginning of man's true life is the fear of God, but the fear of God cannot dwell in a soul that is scattered after external things.

12.6.4.en: * The fear of God is the beginning of virtue, and it is said to be the offspring of faith. It is planted in the heart when a person withdraws his thought from the distraction of the world in order to confine it in the depth of contemplation and in the things to come.

12.6.5.en: * Those who fear God, beloved, persevere with joy in keeping the commandments, even if the matter requires striving and toil, and they expose themselves to dangers for the sake of this pursuit of theirs. The Giver of life has confined the perfection of the commandments, their core, and concentrated them in two that embrace all: love of God, and a similar love, which is love of His icon.

12.6.6.en: * The commandments of God surpass all the treasures of the world. He who possesses them inwardly finds the Lord in them. And he who goes to his chamber continually while meditating on God, God takes him as His own aide; and for him who longs to fulfill the will of God, the angels of heaven become guides.

12.6.7.en: * There is no person in whom sin continues, as long as he walks in the way of the Lawgiver (God) and practices His commandments. For this reason our Lord promised in the Gospels that He abides with whoever keeps His commandments.

12.6.8.en: St. Isaac the Syrian * Acquire for yourself, O disciple, the love of carrying out the commandment, that you may be worthy to receive divine love.

12.6.9.en: * Do you desire to see the ray of the Holy Trinity in your soul? Keep the commandments of Christ.

12.6.10.en: * If a person does not see the sun, he does not enjoy its light; so if a person does not acquire the keeping of the commandments of our Lord, he does not delight in His light.

12.6.11.en: * The door of heaven and the door of the heart are one; if we guard our heart by keeping the commandments of Christ, the door of heaven is opened to us, for the One who dwells in us is the One who dwells in heaven.
